criteria.text: The response identifies that the environmental representations survive only nine months after Closing under APA Section 9.1, while APA Section 7.6 bars Buyer from invasive or subsurface sampling at the Tilden facility until the permit transfer is approved, which may take up to twelve months, so the representations can expire before Buyer is able to test the site. It locates the issue in the APA (Section 9.1 and/or Section 7.6), explains why this matters to Glarol, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that Escrow Agreement Section 12.1 chooses New York law and Manhattan courts, and that because APA Section 11.12 lets the Escrow Agreement control Escrow Fund and Claim Notice disputes, escrow disputes would be split from the Delaware-law, Court of Chancery indemnity disputes under the APA. It locates the issue in the Escrow Agreement (Section 12.1) and/or APA Section 11.12, explains why this matters to Glarol, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that Ostrander's consent to assignment of the Feedstock Supply Agreement was not obtained at Closing, and that the APA neither made that consent a closing condition (Schedule 8.2(d)) nor protected Buyer beyond Seller's limited 90-day efforts and pass-through obligation under Section 2.6, so Glarol does not hold assigned rights to the contract. It locates the issue in the Bill of Sale Annex A and/or the APA (Section 2.6 or Schedule 8.2(d)), explains why this matters to Glarol, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the 30-day period under APA Section 2.5(b) to deliver a Notice of Disagreement on the Closing Statement received July 20, 2026 expired on or about August 19, 2026, before the August 27, 2026 board consent authorized an objection, so Seller can treat the Closing Statement (including the disputed inventory valuation) as final and binding under Section 2.5(c). It locates the issue in the board consent and/or APA Section 2.5, explains why this matters to Glarol, and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Closing Date was June 1, 2026.
The response states that the indemnity escrow amount is $4,200,000.
The response states that the APA is governed by Delaware law.
The response is in memo form and presents the issues ordered by significance to the client, giving for each issue a document and section reference, why it matters, and a recommended fix.
The response claims that Glarol's Notice of Disagreement on the Closing Statement can still be timely delivered within the 30-day period under APA Section 2.5(b).

The response claims that APA Section 11.12 makes the APA's Delaware governing law and forum provisions prevail over the Escrow Agreement's New York provisions for disputes over the Escrow Fund or Claim Notices.
hints: APA prevails over the Escrow Agreement
